rules.title: Statewide rent cap (Civil Code 1947.12)
rules.requirement: Over any 12-month period, an owner may not raise the gross rental rate by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, measured from the lowest rate charged in the prior 12 months, and in no more than two increments for the same tenant. The owner may set the initial rent for a new tenancy freely and must give notice of increases in accordance with Section 827.
rules.key_value: 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.coverage_text: Residential real property (any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including units in a mobilehome park), applying to increases after the initial rental rate of a tenancy has been set.

rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or K-12 school; housing under a local rent control that restricts increases to less than this section; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless a mobilehome; separately alienable property (e.g., single-family home or condo) whose owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, provided tenants received the required written exemption notice; a two-unit structure where the owner occupied one unit as principal residence at the start of the tenancy and continues to, and neither unit is an ADU or junior ADU; homeowners of a mobilehome. Initial rent for a new tenancy is not subject to the cap.
rules.penalty: Owner who demands, accepts, receives or retains rent above the maximum is liable in a civil action for injunctive relief, damages equal to the excess, reasonable attorney's fees and costs in the court's discretion, and up to three times the excess for willful conduct or oppression, fraud or malice; the Attorney General and city attorney or county counsel may enforce and seek injunctive relief. Actions must be brought within three years.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.
rules.interaction_text: Housing subject to rent or price control through a public entity’s valid exercise of its police power consistent with Chapter 2.7 (commencing with Section 1954.50) that restricts annual increases in the rental rate to an amount less than that provided in subdivision (a).
